topPRs.title: cannon: bound preimage oracle requests
topPRs.author: obiyang
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Bound Cannon preimage requests and hint acknowledgements with a configurable `--oracle-timeout` (10 minutes by default).

## Problem
The existing 15-second polling interval only detects host exit. A live host that logs a failed request without responding can stall VM execution indefinitely.

## Solution
Give each request one deadline across all protocol phases, and cap file polling at that deadline. Recover timeout errors when the host has no process exit state yet, so the VM returns an error instead of panicking during recovery. Successful preimage bytes and the wire protocol are unchanged; operators can increase the timeout for slower hosts.

## Testing
- `go test -race ./cannon/cmd ./op-preimage` passed.
- `just go_test './cmd/... ./mipsevm/exec/... ./mipsevm/versions/...'` in `cannon` passed.
- `go test ./op-challenger/kvstore ./op-challenger/game/fault/preimages ./op-challenger/game/fault/trace/utils ./op-challenger/game/fault/trace/alphabet ./op-challenger/game/fault/trace/vm` passed.
- `just lint-go` passed with zero issues and clean module tidiness.
- CLI smoke run with the supported version-8 state and `--stop-at '=0'` passed. Regression tests fail when the request timeout, file deadline cap, or nil-state guard is removed.

## Related Issue
Fixes #15395

topPRs.title: cannon: fail on a misaligned clock_gettime pointer
topPRs.author: methakon
topPRs.body:
Fixes #13442.

## Description

`MIPS64.sol` masked the `clock_gettime` pointer with `ADDRESS_MASK` before validating the memory proof:

```solidity
uint64 effAddr = a1 & arch.ADDRESS_MASK;
```

`ADDRESS_MASK` is `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8`, which clears exactly the low three bits that `EXT_MASK` (`0x7`) inspects. `MIPS64Memory.isValidProof` and `writeMem` both revert with `InvalidAddress` when a misaligned address reaches them, so masking the address first means the alignment check can never fire on this path. A misaligned pointer was silently aligned, and the `timespec` was written at a different address than the guest asked for.

This handler writes two consecutive 64-bit words (`secs` at `effAddr`, `nsecs` at `effAddr + 8`), so a misaligned pointer is invalid and the existing memory-layer check is the correct place to catch it. Using the address as supplied restores that.

## Scope

The other three uses of `ADDRESS_MASK` in this file are left alone, because there the aligned address is the correct MIPS64 behaviour rather than a masked pointer:

- `loadSubWord` / `storeSubWord` implement unaligned sub-word access, which the ISA requires
- `syscallGetRandom` needs the containing word address

## Tests

`test/cannon/MIPS64Memory.t.sol` gains two cases in the existing `MIPS64Memory_IsValidProof_Test` suite:

- `test_isValidProof_misalignedAddress_reverts` — a misaligned address is rejected with `InvalidAddress`, which is the behaviour the syscall now relies on
- `test_addressMaskHidesMisalignment_succeeds` — asserts `ADDRESS_MASK` clears the bits `EXT_MASK` inspects, which is why masking cannot be used here

`forge test --match-path "test/cannon/*"` passes (65 tests), as does the full `forge test` suite (2372 passed, 0 failed, 149 skipped).
